searchText: We've been running Rayonism from a branch of Lighthouse that's intended for spec version `v1.0.x` and IIUC those vectors are for `v1.1.x`. We're figuring out the best way for us to be able to run them, but there might be a bit of delay on our end. the `merge` related objects are branched off phase 0, not altair if that's the main concern It turns out it was way easier than I expected. We're passing all the tests now, just need to make sure we haven't missed any new ones. Exactly. The Altair and Merge specs are still parallel. 1.1.0 prerelease is compatible with Rayonism The differences are really just snappy and removal of some test types. `CONFIG_NAME` is gone too We're looking to add execution payload tests. There's an example test case and addition to the operations table in the test format. Then there are more test cases in another WIP PR About config_name: I think that for the 1.1.0 release we'll revisit the config format. No breaking changes in terms of variable naming, but bundling some subset of constants to only ever be compile-time, and switchable with a single config var, instead of spelling them all out in runtime configuration. cool is it intentional that `CONFIG_NAME` isn't present in the alpha.4-pre2 tests? Yes It's part of the dev branch changes; removing the duplicate all together We could name the compile-time thing "preset" or "bundle" or something. The runtime chain config should really be fully configurable, and behave the same between all clients yeah, i hear you on unifying the usage of it. just wanted to make sure the break is intentional cause i need to deal with it to get these tests to pass I can draft a concept config spec tomorrow morning. And we can discuss on the implementer call. I want to avoid breaking changes as much as possible, but at the same time remove the pain of that config_name var (duplicate between phases, different undocumented side effects per client) and separate compile time configuration from runtime configuration. That should help testnet setup ease + Hive testing (others are working on this, and chain configuration was one of their main struggles) I'll get our Rayonism branch to duck-type it based on slots per epoch. We managed to pass all the tests without requiring any changes to consensus code, which was cool. I'm working on a PR now so that the new test format runs nicely with CI. No need to update our docker image, really. We were debating internally in Nethermind if we can run eth2:eth1 nodes in n:m ratio instead of 1:1 and we think we can. The only thing we would need to change is to spin up BlockTree per eth2 client and later differentiate them in API (merge API as well as standard JSON RPC API). They could share block, receipt and state database (with each having their own block tree, thus head, thus state root). One more thing to extend would be transaction pool which can be shared only partially, but that's not that big of a deal. The only problem if eth2 clients would branch a lot our Databases would be bigger than in 1:1 to accomodate all the variations. this currently isn't a priority for us, but we might implement it before or after the merge if there is demand

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: We've been running Rayonism from a branch of Lighthouse that's intended for spec version `v1.0.x` and IIUC those vectors are for `v1.1.x`. We're figuring out the best way for us to be able to run them, but there might be a bit of delay on our end.

excerpts.content: the `merge` related objects are branched off phase 0, not altair if that's the main concern

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: It turns out it was way easier than I expected. We're passing all the tests now, just need to make sure we haven't missed any new ones.

excerpts.content: Exactly. The Altair and Merge specs are still parallel. 1.1.0 prerelease is compatible with Rayonism

excerpts.author: lukaszrozmej
excerpts.content:
We were debating internally in Nethermind if we can run eth2:eth1 nodes in n:m ratio instead of 1:1 and we think we can. The only thing we would need to change is to spin up BlockTree per eth2 client and later differentiate them in API (merge API as well as standard JSON RPC API). They could share block, receipt and state database (with each having their own block tree, thus head, thus state root). One more thing to extend would be transaction pool which can be shared only partially, but that's not that big of a deal.

The only problem if eth2 clients would branch a lot our Databases would be bigger than in 1:1 to accomodate all the variations.
